engineeringPrinciples.parameter: Gor'kov Primary Acoustic Radiation Force & Contrast Factor (Φ)
engineeringPrinciples.significance: Acoustic standing waves exert direct radiation pressure on suspended droplets. Because plant lipids possess lower density and higher compressibility than aqueous vegetative water, the acoustic contrast factor Φ is strongly positive (+0.26 to +0.29), driving suspended oil micro-droplets toward the acoustic pressure velocity nodes where local droplet concentration increases by >250-fold.

engineeringPrinciples.parameter: Secondary Bjerknes Forces & Orthogonal Acoustic Coalescence
engineeringPrinciples.equation: F_B = - (2π ρ_f / d²) * R1³ R2³ * ω² * (P_a1 P_a2) * cos(θ)
engineeringPrinciples.significance: Dual orthogonal frequencies (1.2 MHz and 2.4 MHz) eliminate stationary nodal stagnation planes. Neighboring droplets oscillating in phase within the acoustic field experience intense secondary Bjerknes attractive forces, which rupture interfacial pectin-protein viscoelastic hydration shells, triggering spontaneous micro-droplet coalescence from d0 < 2.5 µm to d > 40 µm.

Buoyancy separation velocity increases quadratically with droplet radius (r²). Enlarging oil droplets from 2 µm to 40 µm increases Stokes creaming velocity by 400x (from 0.004 mm/s to 1.65 mm/s), enabling rapid continuous laminar decanting without high-G centrifuges that generate shear heat and oxidize delicate phenolics.

engineeringPrinciples.parameter: Specific Energy Consumption (SEC) & Decarbonized Cold Refining
engineeringPrinciples.significance: Continuous acoustophoretic demulsification consumes only 0.25–0.44 kWh/m³ of processed slurry, delivering a 76–88% reduction in electrical power consumption compared to disc-stack centrifuges (which require 2.2–3.8 kWh/m³) while operating strictly at ambient cold-press temperatures (18–28°C).
